name: Neovim
note: This file is a DELTA against catalog/vim.json, which already fully covers Vim's own Normal/Insert/Visual/Command-line commands (Neovim inherits all of those unchanged). Nothing below repeats a shared Vim command; every entry here is something Nvim's own :help vim_diff.txt "Default mappings" section (*default-mappings*, https://neovim.io/doc/user/vim_diff.html rendered the same content but returned no readable body to WebFetch/curl in this session, so the raw runtime/doc/vim_diff.txt source on GitHub was used instead) documents as created unconditionally at startup that Vim does not have, plus the doc pages the *default-mappings* tags point into: diagnostic.txt (*diagnostic-defaults*: ]d [d ]D [D CTRL-W_d), quickfix.txt (*[q* *]q* *[Q* *]Q* *[_CTRL-Q* *]_CTRL-Q* *[l* *]l* *[L* *]L* *[_CTRL-L* *]_CTRL-L*), tagsrch.txt (*]t* *[t* *[T* *]T* *]_CTRL-T* *[_CTRL-T*), editing.txt (*]a* *[a* *[A* *]A*), windows.txt (*]b* *[b* *[B* *]B*), insert.txt (*[<Space>* *]<Space>*), pattern.txt (*v_star-default* *v_#-default*), various.txt (*CTRL-L-default*, *gO*, *gc-default* *gcc-default* *v_gc-default*, *K-lsp-default*), change.txt (*Y-default*, *&-default*, *gr-default*), motion.txt (*dir-mappings*, the "-" key), lsp.txt (*lsp-defaults* GLOBAL DEFAULTS: gra gri grn grr grt grx i_CTRL-S), and treesitter.txt (*treesitter-defaults*). Also included: repeat.txt's *mcursor*/*multicursor* COMMANDS section, which redefines "Q" and its neighbours as built-in Normal/Visual-mode commands (not phrased as *default-mappings* tags, but unconditional built-in bindings all the same, and this is the single biggest behavioral difference from Vim's "Q" = Ex mode); and terminal.txt's Input section, which documents CTRL-\ CTRL-N and CTRL-\ CTRL-O as the built-in way out of Terminal-mode (catalog/vim.json's own note says it deliberately left out Terminal-Job mode entirely, so this is not a duplicate). Left out on purpose: gc{motion} and the Operator-pending "gc" text object (o_gc-default) both require an arbitrary motion/operator argument, excluded the same way vim.json excludes d{motion}; v_@-default (Visual "@{register}") requires a register argument, excluded the same way vim.json has no "@" entries; i_CTRL-U/i_CTRL-W's documented addition ("sets a new undo point before deleting") is a behavioral tweak to keys vim.json already lists with the same chord, not a new binding, so it is not duplicated here; <C-LeftMouse> (mcursor-mouse) is mouse-only; the ALT-h/j/k/l and CTRL-R terminal-mode window-navigation/paste snippets shown in terminal.txt's Input section are `:tnoremap`/`:inoremap` examples for users to add themselves, not shipped defaults, so no Terminal-mode CTRL-W bindings are invented; "g CTRL-A" during a multicursor session reuses a chord catalog/vim.json already lists (Normal: dump memory profile; Visual: sequential increment) with a third, count-dependent meaning layered on top, so it is called out here rather than duplicated as a fourth ambiguous entry; "[count]Q" (place a cursor at every search match) is a count-modified use of the plain "Q" toggle already listed below. The result is intentionally short: Neovim's default keymap is overwhelmingly the same as Vim's, and most of what changes at the default-key level is either version/LSP/treesitter-gated behavior layered onto existing Vim keys (K, CTRL-L, "gr", "an"/"in" fall back to LSP when Treesitter is inactive) rather than brand-new chords, or, like the multicursor and Terminal-mode entries here, genuinely new but few in number. Version: current Nvim master docs as of 2026-09-04; some entries (LSP gra/gri/.../grx, the multicursor Q family) are recent additions and may not exist in older Neovim releases.
